gallery.filename: Agia Paraskevi - Agia Ekaterini - Agios Nikolaos Church, Mykonos, Greece (53505698357).jpg
gallery.title: File:Agia Paraskevi - Agia Ekaterini - Agios Nikolaos Church, Mykonos, Greece (53505698357).jpg
gallery.artist: Warren LeMay from Chicago, IL, United States
gallery.description: One of the many Cycladic-style churches in the Mykonos Chora, or main town, this church is dedicated to the saints Paraskevi, Ekaterini, and Nikolaos, with each saint having a separate gabled nave, campanile, and doorway.  The limewashed building is typical of the architecture of Mykonos and the Cyclades, and today remains in use as a Greek Orthodox Church.

gallery.title: File:Abandoned Building, Mykonos, Greece (53496785739).jpg
gallery.artist: Warren LeMay from Chicago, IL, United States
gallery.description: The Cycladic houses of the island of Mykonos take after other islands in the Cyclades, with white stucco exteriors, white or colorful trim, low-slope roofs enclosed by parapets, and casement windows.  The islands, one of the most scenic parts of Greece, are known for this style of architecture, which is found throughout Mykonos.

gallery.title: File:Aegean Maritime Museum Greece (53504496647).jpg
gallery.artist: Warren LeMay from Chicago, IL, United States
gallery.description: Built in the mid-19th Century, this vernacular Cycladic-style house was constructed for a middle-class family in the Mykonos Chora, or main town.  The house features a limewashed exterior with stone trim at the windows and doorways, casement windows, and an interior that has been restored to its original interior.  The building today has been restored and opened to the public as a museum that interprets the history of Mykonos.
